subject: Asynchronous Shiny exchange for long-running calculations?

messages.author: 7f3dcb786c576e61
messages.subject: Asynchronous Shiny exchange for long-running calculations?
parts:
Hi,

I really like the ease of use that Shiny offers and it is easy to get started. I have found OpenCPU better when I need more flexibility and control. I also think I need it for long-running calculations in R where I can get partial results and would like the front/app to update with intermediate results. 

An example is long-running bayesian calculations in R such as with the BEST package; here I would like graphs that update with, say, every 1000 samples from the MCMC chains until a large number of total samples has been taken.

Are there any examples of people using Shiny for this type of (multiple) asynchronous data exchanges between the ui and server side?

Thanks,

Robert Feldt

messages.subject: Re: Asynchronous Shiny exchange for long-running calculations?
parts:
I have sort of a similar case where I want to update a progress bar. I managed by using invalidateLater()

An example of breaking up a long loop

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  counter <- reactiveValues(start=0, end=0)
  observe({
    input$actionButton
    counter$start <<- 1
    counter$end <<- input$nIteration
  })
  results <- reactive({
    if(counter$start == 0) return(NULL)
    if(counter$start >= counter$end) {
      counter$start <<- 0
      counter$end <<- 0
      return(NULL)
    }
    batchSize <- ifelse(input$batchSize > counter$end-counter$start, counter$end-counter$start, input$batchSize)
    ans <- list()
    for(i in 1:batchSize) {
      ans[[i]] <- rnorm() ### This should be a real computation
    }
    counter$start <<- counter$start+batchSize
    invalidateLater(1, session)
    return(ans)
  })
  output$result <- reactive({results()})
})

The actual computation should of course be meaningful but in this way you can cut up long running calculations and perform things such as sending results in small chunks or updating some other outputs...

best

Thomas

parts:
Thanks Thomas!

Based on your example code I have been able to experiment. But I cannot get the ui to update during the looping. I must be missing something. When running the code below the output of count and result is frozen while the looping is going on. I need it to update between loop rounds.

Hmm,

Robert

library(shiny)

ui <- basicPage(
  tags$p(actionButton("increment", "+1")),
  tags$p(actionButton("decrement", "-1")),
  tags$p(actionButton("step", "Step count")),
  uiOutput("count"),
  textOutput("result")
)

max_steps <- 40
step_size <- 3

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  values <- reactiveValues(i = 1, isCounting = FALSE, endCount = NULL)
  
  output$count <- renderText({
    paste0("i = ", values$i)
  })
  
  observe({
    input$increment    
    values$i <- isolate({values$i}) + 1
  })
  
  observe({
    input$decrement
    values$i <- isolate({values$i}) - 1
  })

  # Start counting on observing input$step
  observe({
    input$step

    isolate({
      values$isCounting <- TRUE
      values$endCount <- values$i + max_steps
    })
  })

  # Counter code that will be invoked when isCounting is first set and then reinvoked
  # until the endCount has been reached.
  counter <- reactive({
    cat("In counter(), i = ", values$i, "\n")
    if(values$isCounting == FALSE) return("Not counting")

    if(values$isCounting == TRUE && values$i >= values$endCount) {
      values$isCounting <- FALSE
      return("Not counting")
    }

    num_steps <- min(step_size, values$endCount - values$i)

    ### Perform real and possible long-running calculation here:
    Sys.sleep(0.25)
    ans <- paste("steps = ", num_steps)
    ###

    values$i <- values$i + num_steps
    invalidateLater(1, session)
    return(ans)
  })

  output$result <- reactive({counter()})
}

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))
